_about: Leads: candidate ciphertexts found by sweeps and not yet vetted. They are not catalogue entries and are not on the site. Each keeps the id it was given at merge (ids are shared with catalogue.json and never reused). A lead is promoted to catalogue.json by `python docs/_check_catalogue.py --promote <id>` once its "vetting" block passes the gate (README Conventions, "Catalogue vetting bar"; field list in docs/_check_catalogue.py); a lead found read, duplicated, readable with a held key or not a cipher is closed with --close and kept here as a record. Entries 861-1422 were moved here from catalogue.json on 28 Oct 2026: all came from the Oct 2026 archive sweeps, scored from descriptions; the 98 checked on 28 Oct (research/verify_2026-10/) keep that check in status and prior_art.

leads.title: Prince Rupert to William Legge, letters in code (Dartmouth papers)
leads.correspondents: Prince Rupert to William Legge (also Digby to Legge)
leads.shelfmark: Staffordshire Record Office, D(W)1778/I/i/37-59
leads.folio_note: 12 items: I/i/37, I/i/39, I/i/45, I/i/48, I/i/46, I/i/47, I/i/49, I/i/53, I/i/54, I/i/55, I/i/56, I/i/59. One on linen (53). Two noted 'not deciphered' (56 Digby, 59 Rupert); 49 'in code, without translation'
leads.status: Staffordshire catalogue: 'in code', several not deciphered. Rupert / Charles I ciphers read by Lasry (SP106-3/5 keys) may apply. Not on DECODE (known.py: no hit). Checked 28 Oct 2026: Not opened in detail (Discovery pages did not render in WebFetch). Search found no decipherment; Warburton (1849) prints some Rupert-Legge letters and should be grepped before ordering images. Printed-edition check, 28 Oct 2026: Partly in print. Eliot Warburton, Memoirs of Prince Rupert and the Cavaliers (1849), 3 vols, Rupert-Legge letters 'from the Earl of Dartmouth's MSS': vol. II pp. 406-408 (April 1644, flagged 'In Cipher', Master of the Horse; letters of 18 and 23 Apr 1644); vol. III pp. 27-28 (Oct 1644, flagged '[In cipher]'); pp. 63-64 and 69-70 (March 1645); pp. 73-74 (Hereford, 31 Mar 1645); p. 100 (Daventry, 8 June 1645); pp. 125-128 (Digby to Legge, answering Legge's of 22 June; Legge's reply, pp. 128-131, cites Digby's letter of 30 June 1645); pp. 151-156 (Bristol, 28-29 July 1645). Staffordshire item dates from the TNA Discovery API (28 Oct 2026): /37 = 30 Apr 1644 (Master of the Horse; matches Warburton II 406-408, whose letters are dated 18 and 23 Apr, so date mismatch), /39 = 10 Oct 1644 (Warburton III 27-28), /41 = 8 Mar 1645 (III 63-64, matched on content), /45 = 31 Mar 1645 (III 73-74, exact date), /54 = 8 June 1645 (III p.100, exact), /56 = Digby 30 June 1645 (III 125-128, printed in full as plain text; the 'coded part not deciphered' is therefore deciphered in print). So six of the twelve items are printed in 1849 with plaintext. Warburton leaves Rupert's own name and some name-cipher groups as '[cipher]' or bare numbers (e.g. '92, 352' in the 29 July 1645 letter, III p.156) and says (II p.471 fn) that he gives uninterpreted ciphers only where he cannot read them. Not located in Warburton: /46 /47 /48 /49 /53 /55 (dates not retrieved) and /59 (Rupert, 9 Aug 1645, 'not deciphered'; the last printed Rupert-Legge letter is 29 July 1645). HMC Dartmouth (1887) calendars only Rupert-Legge letters of 1661. Verdict: lead is mostly closed for 37/39/41/45/54/56; items 59 and probably 46-49, 53, 55 remain unprinted, and the printed ones give plaintext cribs for the Rupert-Legge key.
leads.why: Rupert's private letters to the Legge circle in the 1644-45 court quarrels, in his own cipher.

XVI (A.D. 1722-1725), Proceedings against Bishop Atterbury: Report of the Committee of the Lords on Plunkett's cypher and the numerical cypher 1378 = Atterbury ('Illington' / 'Jones'); glosses of cant names (e.g. 'barrels' = army, 'brokers' = lord Marr); decipherers' evidence incl. The trial volume prints the committee's findings, the interpretations of cant names and the decipherers' testimony, but not the SP 35 letters as figure strings with plaintext, nor the numeral cypher tables of SP 35/47/52 or 35/73/52 as tables (glosses only). SP 35/46/59 'undecyphered paper' is not identified in it. Cruickshanks and Erskine-Hill 2004 not accessible online. OCR of the BSB scan is poor. Lead stays open for the figure-string letters; the printed glosses are a partial vocabulary for Plunket's cypher.

leads.status: Existing (printed): the 34 autograph letters (Milan, Bicocca, Pavia, Genoa, Vigevano, 4 Jan - 15 Dec 1522) are printed in E. Pacheco y de Leyva, La política española en Italia. Correspondencia de D. Fernando Marín, abad de Nájera, con Carlos I, t. I (1521-1524), Madrid 1919, nos. 48-106, cipher passages given in clear and marked (cifra)/(claro); archive.org 'lapoliticaespa01pach' (public domain). Images seen 4 Nov 2026 (BDH CC BY 4.0 PDF, issue #250): contemporary claros attached to several letters (Cartas 1, 9, 19 separate 'Claro' sheet; Carta 8 claro only; Carta 11 interlinear, Carta 20 marginal decipherment; Carta 9 also a 19th-century copy headed 'Clave'/'Claro'). The system is the abbot's own nomenclator (3-4 lowercase letter groups such as bux, rub, tef, frod, plus signs); it is not the Sessa 1524 system (0 of 21 sure Sessa values and 1 of 34 groups in common). Still unseen: the 'contracifra' copy in carpeta 8, a possible check key for an imperial cipher of 1522. Earlier note: BNE catalogue: the 8th folder holds a copy of the key ('contracifra'). Related to the repo's lopehurtado1523 target (its 'Claro' leaf is the Abbot of Nájera's). No decipherment of the ciphered letters noted beyond the key copy; the first 12 letters are in print (Pacheco). Checked 28 Oct 2026: Nájera's cipher Ko.3 is reconstructed (Kolosova) and the volume holds a key copy; the letters themselves are not found read. Related repo target lopehurtado1523.
leads.why: A key copy in hand for a 1522 imperial cipher; reads the Nájera letters and may match other 1522 ciphers in the repo.

leads.title: Filippo Maria Visconti, Duke of Milan → Francesco Sforza, six cipher letters on parchment, Nov-Dec 1446
leads.correspondents: Filippo Maria Visconti, Duke of Milan → Count Francesco Sforza (his son-in-law)
leads.folio_note: DECODE R7902 (f. 110, 2 pp.; Mazzatinti: Milan 1 Nov, DECODE 10 Nov), R7903 (f. 112, 7 Nov), R7904 (f. 130, c. 26 Nov), R7907 (f. 136, 29 Nov), R7914 (f. 154, 12 Dec, 2 pp.), R7915 (f. 158, Cusago 31 Dec); one page each, graphic signs + letters + numerals. Mazzatinti marks each 'In cifre: membr.' and lists f. 131 as 'Traduzione della lettera precedente' (a contemporary translation of f. 130). f. 145 (Duke, 1 Dec, in cifre) is not on DECODE.
leads.status: DECODE Non-decrypted (all six; DECODE gives no sender or receiver, identified here from Mazzatinti). leads.title: Feliciano Montenegro (New Orleans) → Manuel Gómez Pedraza, War Minister: cipher letter on the Cuba project, with an undeciphered duplicate

leads.status: CEHM: the summary gives the content (ships of Gordon & Forstall, buying vessels "for the cause", news from Havana of troops leaving Cádiz), so the original was deciphered; the duplicate is in cipher. Verdict read; useful only as evidence of the system.

leads.title: Mosén Pedro Vara → Ferdinand, king of Sicily: letter from Dueñas in mixed clear and cipher with interlinear glosses
leads.correspondents: Pedro de Vara → Ferdinand II of Aragon

leads.status: Existing: contemporary interlinear decipherment on the document (images seen 4 Nov 2026, BDH CC BY 4.0 PDF, issue #250). Every ciphered passage on ff. 1-2 is glossed in Castilian in a smaller, quicker hand, continuing in the margins where the interline is too short; some glosses struck out and rewritten, so decipherment done on the original (e.g. 'onze leguas', 'el rey de Portogal', 'el conde de Benavente', 'el almirante', 'el señor arçobispo de Toledo'; group 'semp v x3gΞ' = 'Señor Príncipe'). No unglossed cipher block seen; at 120 dpi two or three very short groups at line starts on f. 2 are covered only by a marginal gloss not read in full. Address on the back 'Al muy alto e muy excelente Señor el Señor Rey', and the Prince and Princess spoken of in the third person: addressee probably John II of Aragon, not Ferdinand. Cipher: digits, Latin letters as signs and special signs, probably with nulls; syllabic/nomenclator, possibly of the d56 family (ferdinand1473) — not checked. Earlier note: BNE card: firma autógrafa, notas marginales. Viewer page 1 seen: signs and digits inside a clear Spanish text, later interlinear glosses in another hand that seem to cover part of it. Not on DECODE; not in the repo. Same place and weeks as Ferdinand → John II, Dueñas 12 Nov 1470 (MSS/20211/56, R9530 solved, targets/ferdinand1473 d56).

prior_art.decode: Not a DECODE item: known.py on the harvested dump for Eldem, AEXSHE0010170 and Sedad Hakki gave only this lead and its sweep rows.
prior_art.tomokiyo: No cryptiana page on Eldem: WebSearch naming the coded diary with cryptiana, Cryptologia and HistoCrypt returned only SALT records and a Schmeh post on another diary.
prior_art.lasry: No Lasry treatment: known.py shows no GL.htm or Lasry row, and the WebSearch naming the diary with the cryptologic venues found none.
prior_art.edition: Decipherment in print, as excerpts: Edhem Eldem, 'Becoming Sedad Hakkı Eldem', essay in Serena Acciai, Sedad Hakkı Eldem. An aristocratic architect and more (Firenze University Press, 2018; open access, archive.org oapen-20.500.12657-55503, full text read), pp. 336-337 and notes pp. 349-350 and after, quotes the diary in English from May 1925 to October 1926. No full text is printed. The 2008 book by Tanyeli, Tanju and Eldem that assigned the AAE codes was not opened: only its press notice is open (SALT 199494).
prior_art.literature: Same essay: 'The coded diary Sedad Hakkı kept in 1925-1926' is cited from the 'author's collection', with AAE 064, 067 and 072 named (all within record 121243, AAE056-115); 38 lines of the OCR cite the coded diary. A grep of the text for decode, decipher and transcribe found no account of the system or of who decoded it. WebSearch found no cryptologic paper.

vetting.key_check: No key seen or held. Edhem Eldem's quotations show the system was read by him or for him; the essay as grepped does not print it.
vetting.duplicates: known.py on Eldem, AEXSHE0010170 and Sedad Hakki, and on 'Becoming Sedad' (no hits): only this lead and research/sweep_2026-11_ottoman_turkish rows; no catalogue entry or target holds the document.
vetting.closed: Edhem Eldem's essay 'Becoming Sedad Hakkı Eldem' in Acciai 2018 (pp. 336-337, notes p. 349 ff.) quotes the coded diary of May 1925-October 1926 in English translation, citing AAE 064, 067, 072. Excerpts only, and the pages AAE038-054 are not cited individually, though they sit in the same notebook. The 2008 catalogue was not opened. Scans are Local Access at SALT, so the unprinted text cannot be worked remotely.

seen.where: Gelders Archief, 0439 Huizen Waardenburg en Neerijnen, inventory row 125 in the viewer at https://www.geldersarchief.nl/bronnen/archieven?mizig=210&miadt=37&miaet=1&micode=0439&minr=4399997&miview=inv2 (read in Chrome); APE record 0439-125 confirms the title.
seen.extent: All 134 scans viewed in this batch, scans 1-134 with none left out, at the same fit-page view as inv. 124 (0.75 or 0.8 of viewer width, a few at full width, scan 10 also zoomed). Viewing covered every scan for digit runs and signs; the running text was not transcribed. Scans that first showed a blank pane, a loading wheel or a blur were reloaded until sharp: 15, 18, 38, 52, 54, 57, 59, 76, 77, 84, 87, 120, 123, 134. None failed to render, including scan 38. Blank or show-through-only versos: 4, 20, 24, 28, 32, 48, 52, 59, 60, 71, 72, 80, 83, 84, 88, 92, 100, 121, 122, 123, 124, 127, 128. Slips laid over a page at 25-29, 105-109 and 130-134 were photographed lifted too, so the text under them is seen. Dutch letters 'Doorluchtigste Prins' signed H. Vere, 's Hage 23 May to 11 Sept 1731, and memoranda ('Memorie'); scans 45-47 a draft letter in French to the King, 'Projet de la lettre que Z pourroit ecrire a N'; scans 125-126, 129-130 French copies (Seville declaration, marquis de la Paz letter); scans 131-133 a draft letter in French.
seen.cipher: No digit runs and no running sign cipher on any of the 134 scans. Clear Dutch with cover names: Z and N throughout, O, E.E., F.F., D:D:, S.S., Y.Y. Isolated code numbers that stand for names or terms, one at a time in clear sentences, on scans including 10 (800, 850), 12 (750), 14 (950, 800, 900), 16 (900), 21 (900), 22 (750), 31 (960, 970, 900), 34 (970, 750), 44 (750), 57 (900, 750), 67 (750), 73, 74 and 94 (750). Single sign ⊞ on scans 11, 15, 22, 55, 66. The writer glosses two numbers himself at scan 31, in a postscript: '960 in de Memorie vermeld is de Heer Borck en 970 de Heer ...'. No interlinear or marginal decipherment.

Scan 15 of the key, headed 'Chyffer' and dated 1 June 1731, and key scan 3 give 750 een Accommodement, 800 De Heer Luisius, 850 De Scheiding, 900 De Heer Grumbkow, 950 Anglois, and key scan 3 ends with 960 and 970 (Borck and a second name), matching Vere's own postscript at scan 31; scan 10 '800' and '850', scan 12 '750 met N' and scan 21 '900' read sensibly with them. Key scan 1: Zyne Hoogheit Z, De Koning van Pruissen N, Chesterfield O; scan 45 'Projet de la lettre que Z pourroit ecrire a N', about the succession of King William, agrees. Key scan 2 gives the sign ⊞ for 'Huiwelyk met Engeland'.
vetting.key_in_volume: Gelders Archief 0439 inv. 126, 'Sleutels tot het geheimschrift, 1730, 1731', 20 scans online: scan 1 'Extract uit het groot Chyffer', scan 2 more names and signs, scans 3 and 15 numbered lists, scan 9 'Supplement du Chiffre' A 42/43 to Z 88/89. vetting.closed: Every scan of the folder viewed, 1-134 of 134, none left unread and none failing to render. They show only clear Dutch and French with cover names, isolated code numbers standing for names and terms (750, 800, 850, 900, 950, 960, 970) and the single sign ⊞. Those spot-tested are glossed by key inv. 126 (scans 1, 2, 3, 15). The inventory's 'gedeeltelijk in geheimschrift' is met by these. leads.title: Sigismondo Lodron → Ferrante Gonzaga, two letters partly in cipher, deciphered between the lines
leads.correspondents: Sigismondo Lodron (Laterano) → Ferrante Gonzaga
leads.shelfmark: Biblioteca Estense Universitaria, Modena, Autografoteca Campori, Lettera L, Lodron Laterano, Sigismondo, cc. 1-3 and cc. 4-6
leads.folio_note: Cipher runs inside the clear text on 1r (one run, glossed 'Ferrara'), 1v (about 6 lines), 4r (4-5 runs), 4v (6-7 runs) and 6r (2-3 runs): about 15 runs, roughly 200-250 signs. Most runs carry a contemporary decipherment written above them; several on 1v, 4r, 4v and 6r have none.
leads.status: Records: 'Lettera parzialmente cifrata (ma decifrata in interlinea).' Not in Dan's data. Manifest uuid(s): 56f7c9f3-6083-4ee1-bd3b-4628f3e25569, 767e3b8d-82f8-4aeb-b4bf-0c869a06f627. Worked by WAINUT on 3 Nov 2026, not solved: pairs located, key started. Signs look like Latin letters (a d e g l m o p x y z), a long s, a double-crossed sign and an E-like sign, not at face value. Two pairs seen by eye ('Don Diego' over 8 signs, 'In Conclavi' over 12 signs) do not fit one simple substitution, so the system is probably homophonic with syllable or null signs. Glossed runs name Salviati, the conclave, 'Don Diego' (presumably Hurtado de Mendoza), Duke Ottavio and the bishop of Pola, which fits Dec 1549. Two machine transcription passes could not be blinded (the gloss sits in the ascender zone of the cipher) and disagree widely; neither is usable. Not the ercole1544 half-shift; the ferrante1549 table does not give 'Don Diego'. A transcription job, not a break.
leads.why: Two letters in one key with interlinear clear; small but complete.
leads.verify: Transcribe each run sign-first on full-size crops, pair it with its gloss, freeze a key on one letter and test it on the other.

leads.title: Axel Oxenstierna → 'Magnifice Vir' (Ludwig Camerarius?), Stockholm 10 June 1625, partly in cipher (two-digit runs, glossed)
leads.correspondents: Axel Oxenstierna → Ludwig Camerarius (?)
leads.shelfmark: Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 10382 (Collectio Camerariana vol. 32), piece 81 on the leaf (Halm prints 'n. 78')
leads.folio_note: MDZ bsb00112117 scans 307-309. The leaf is numbered 81. Halm's entry stands between n. 80 and n. 82 and prints 'n. 78', evidently a misprint.
leads.status: Key note (Brice Dudout, 5 Nov 2026) (the classification already matches the 4 Nov vetting: existing, contemporary interlinear decipherment over all 21 runs). The key rebuilt from the glosses is a homophonic table in alternating alphabetical blocks: consonants 1-18 ascending (b1 c2 d3 ... t15), vowels 19-23 (a e i o u), vowels 26-30 descending (u o i e a), 31-35 ascending, 38-42 descending, consonants 60 down to 43 and 61-78 ascending, e = 80. Predictions from the structure check out on the leaf (m = 9, h = 6 in 'marchiam'; b = 1 in 'Brandeburgica'). It is not Lasry's Rusdorff 1625 table (A = 16/40/64) and not the 1621-22 Camerarius nomenclator. Printed text not checked: AOSB part 1 may print the letter from the Stockholm draft. Earlier note: Halm, Verzeichniss der handschriftlichen Sammlung der Camerarii (1874), p. 60: 'n. 78 Axelii ab Oxenstierna ep. (ad Lud. Cam.?) 10 Jun. 1625 (partim signis secretis scripta)'. Addressed 'Magnifice Vir', dated at Stockholm, signed by Oxenstierna.
leads.why: Oxenstierna on the Danish and Brandenburg proposals and Sweden's choice between Poland and Germany in 1625. The glosses give a two-digit key sample.
leads.score_note: Scored from Halm's entry and the three leaves, 4 Nov 2026

leads.title: Gyorgy II Rakoczi, Prince of Transylvania, to Charles X Gustav of Sweden: Latin letters with sign-cipher passages (Polish campaign of 1657)
leads.correspondents: Gyorgy II Rakoczi (Georgius Rakoczy) -> Charles X Gustav, King of Sweden
leads.shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Turcica, bihang Transylvanica, SE/RA/2119/2119.5/4 ("Furstarnas av Siebenbürgen Georg I och II Rácóczis originalbrev till Kungl. Maj:t", 1632-1659), images 18, 20, 22, 23
leads.folio_note: 64 images (R0003533). Images 18 (5 sign lines), 20 (about 6 sign lines in a letter about "Rex Poloniae"), 22 (4 sign lines) and 23 (a full page of about 16 lines of signs, about 500 characters, with a faint Latin gloss between some rows).
leads.status: Existing, not 'partly read' (Brice Dudout, 5 Nov 2026). (a) The contemporary interlinear Latin decipherment covers every sign row: the glosses run about two rows behind the cipher, so the rows that look unglossed (top and bottom of image 23) are glossed further down. Checked by deciphering the 'unglossed' rows of image 23 with a key built from image 18 alone: '...[ex]creverit, an Vestra Majestas possit partem aliquam exercitus sui ad Cracoviam pro conjunctione expedire. Caetera magnificus dominus Sternbach Majestati Vestrae uberius perscribet', which matches the gloss and the edition word for word. (b) All three cipher postscripts are printed deciphered in Szilágyi Sándor, Erdély és az északkeleti háború. Levelek és okiratok II (MTA, Budapest 1891; archive.org erdlysazsz02sziluoft): PS of 12 Dec 1656 (image 18) p. 204; PS of 28 Dec 1656 (image 20) p. 209; PS of 27 Feb 1657 (images 22-23) p. 275. (c) The same volume holds a fourth sign-cipher letter (images 52-53, Gyalu, 13 Jan 1658), printed in full on pp. 484-485 ('Eredetije titkos írással írva a svéd állami levéltárban'): also existing. (d) A sign key rebuilt from image 18 (simple substitution, Latin, about 22 signs) was validated on image 20 held out: 0.935 of characters against a best of 0.442 for 200 shuffled keys. The key is not printed in Szilágyi and could be filed as a key record. Possible new leads in the same volume, not checked: image 8 (Georg I, 23 Apr 1644, number cipher in a Latin letter) and images 62-63 (1659, dense number cipher). Earlier note: Catalogue: only "originalbrev" of the two Rakoczi princes; no cipher mentioned. Graphic sign cipher, probably monoalphabetic (the Lang repertory describes the same prince's sign systems in MOL E 190 as "not broken"). A few glosses are written between the rows at image 23, so a partial reading was made at the time. Not in Lang's repertory (checked pp. 191-330 for Swedish-archive items); keys for the same fonds are held (DECODE R4310 "Siebenbürgen Schauis" number key and R4296, Chifferklaver låda II), but they are number keys, not sign keys.
leads.why: Rakoczi's alliance with Charles X Gustav against Poland (Jan 1657): the sign-cipher passages carry the secret terms between the two allies.
leads.verify: View images 18-25 at full size; transcribe the signs, align with the partial glosses on image 23, test as a monoalphabetic sign cipher in Latin; check MOL E 190 sign tables (Lang T.Rag) and the printed Swedish-archive editions of the Rakoczi-Charles X letters.

vetting.closed: Real graphic sign cipher in Latin letters (Riksarkivet R0003533 images 18-23), already read: the contemporary interlinear Latin decipherment covers every sign row (glosses run about two rows behind the cipher, checked on the apparently unglossed rows of image 23 against a key built from image 18), and all three cipher postscripts are printed deciphered in Szilagyi Sandor, Erdely es az eszakkeleti haboru II (Budapest 1891), pp. 204, 209, 275; a fourth sign-cipher letter (images 52-53, 13 Jan 1658) is printed on pp. 484-485. Verdict corrected from partly_read on 5 Nov 2026 (Brice Dudout, PR #273). Not a lead for a new reading; a sign key rebuilt from image 18 (0.935 on held-out image 20) could be filed as a key record.

leads.folio_note: Scan 10: numerical cipher, groups of 1-4 digits (e.g. '1460. 1614. 112. 172. 6. 102'), about 540 groups, signed by the prince and two other hands. The inventory says Fagel's transcription is folded in the letter. inv. 9 holds no other ciphered letter.

The three clear letters in the same file carry the same note (pp. 162, 184, 185). Only the cipher key may be new: a William III-Fagel numerical nomenclator, with Fagel's decipherment sheet, which could be rebuilt from this cipher/clear pair and applied to other William III <-> Fagel ciphers (e.g. the Royal House Archives, KHA). Related, also digitised and partly in cipher: 3.01.18 inv. 385-400 (Paets, Chieze, Heemskerck, Madrid 1672-86; same legation as battier1686) and inv. 346-370 (Wijngaerden, Van Haren, Wolfsen, Rumpf, Mortaigne; Denmark/Sweden 1672-87); inv. 370 (Mortaigne 1675-76) shows no cipher on a pass through its 42 scans. The States General copies in the catalogue (nos. 376, 377) are physical only.

leads.correspondents: Cardinal Pascual de Aragón <-> Pedro de Aragón; also the count of Medellín and Juan José de Austria
leads.shelfmark: BNE Mss/2043 (olim G. 85), 682 ff.; BDH bdh0000042925
leads.folio_note: Folios approximate (PDF page minus 2-4, read on a few leaves). f. 353 (read): 'Descifrado de las cartas de los numeros 31 a 84', a run of clear copies headed 'Carta del Cardenal mi S.r para el S.r D. Pedro...' (PDF pp. 0356-0373). Ciphered letters with the clear in the margin seen at about ff. 135-137, 482 and 498; the Inventario also lists ff. 459, 501, 590, 595, 636, 638 'descifradas al margen y a continuacion'. Wholly in cipher, no clear seen: about ff. 25-35, 50-53, 59-81, 214-233, and more. About 90-110 ciphered pieces, counted on thumbnails (plus or minus 20 %).
leads.status: From the printed BNE Inventario general (not in the Europeana/BDH notices of the earlier sweep). Views checked on thumbnails and a few close-ups, 4 Nov 2026. The 'Descifrado 31-84' is a period decipherment: clear copies of about 50 letters, not yet paired with the ciphered letters. The ciphered letters seen all use one system: a mixed syllabic cipher of 1-2 digit numbers, letter- and syllable-signs and a few 3-digit codes. Our key from two marginal pairs did not validate (0.70 against a 0.85 threshold; shuffled-key control 0.46), so no reading is claimed. The Inventario's f. 34 note on 'el n.o 121 en la cifra del conde de Medellin' points to other keys; not found in close-up.
leads.why: The cardinal's letters to his brother in the years of Valenzuela and Juan José's coup (1675-77), with period decipherments that can give the key for the many letters left in cipher.
leads.score_note: Scored from the Inventario general and a thumbnail pass with a few close-ups, 4 Nov 2026 (research/dudout_leads_2026-11-04/, issue #254)

leads.title: Count of Monterrey, the Constable of Castile and Francisco de Borja → the Duke of Villahermosa: letters in four ciphers, several with period translations
leads.correspondents: Count of Monterrey; Constable of Castile; Francisco de Borja → Duke of Villahermosa (governor of the Spanish Netherlands from 1675)
leads.folio_note: Folios approximate unless read. Pairs with a period clear in vol. 1 (Mss/2408): Monterrey, Brussels 30 Mar 1674, ff. 190-191v and a second ciphered copy, with 'Copia de carta de S.E. ... [desci]frada por el Duque, Brujas a 1.o de abril 1674' (ff. 192-193v, read); Monterrey, Brussels 8 Apr 1674 (clear f. 249, read) and 14 Apr 1674 ('Copia de carta ...'); Monterrey, Aranjuez 8 May 1675, clear in the margin (f. 139v); Constable, Madrid 11 Sep 1675, separate translation (f. 118, read). Borja, Madrid 1679 (both vols.): marginal glosses on part of the blocks only (about 15-30 % of the cipher). Ciphered with no clear seen: Monterrey 1674 (about ff. 175-177, 247-248, 260-263, 273-288, 330-338), Constable (vol. 1 f. 50; vol. 2 ff. 66, 79, 100-101, 107, 113-114 and two long runs), Monterrey 1675 (ff. 147-149), Borja 20 Dec 1673 (vol. 2 ff. 1-3) and 1679 (vol. 1 ff. 375-377). Group counts are rough visual estimates.
leads.status: From the printed BNE Inventario general. Views checked on thumbnails and close-ups, 4 Nov 2026. The pairs listed in folio_note are period decipherments or translations (existing). Four systems, none of them the one of Mss/2043: Monterrey, Brussels 1674 (numbers 1-3 digits with isolated letter-signs, struck-through numbers probably nulls); Constable, Madrid 1673-75 (1-2 digit numbers with vowel-consonant digraphs); Monterrey, Madrid/Aranjuez 1675 (numbers with written syllables); Borja, Madrid 1673 and 1679 (dotted numbers with a nomenclator in thousands). The Inventario's 'Monterrey 1674 (siege of Oudenaarde) con su traduccion', 'Borja 18 Apr 1679 con su traduccion' and 'Constable 25 Oct 1673 con su traduccion' were not found as such. Rough extent left in cipher with no clear seen: 5,000-7,000 groups (Monterrey 1674), 3,000-4,000 (Constable), about 700 (Monterrey 1675), about 1,300 (Borja). No key built yet.
leads.why: The Madrid court and the governor in Brussels writing in cipher during the Dutch War (1673-79); the period translations can give four keys for the letters left unread.
leads.score_note: Scored from the Inventario general and a thumbnail pass with close-ups, 4 Nov 2026 (research/dudout_leads_2026-11-04/, issue #254)
leads.verify: Rebuild the Monterrey 1674 key from the 30 Mar 1674 pair (two ciphered copies of the same text) and test it on 8 and 14 Apr; then the Constable key from 11 Sep 1675; read the letters with no clear.
leads.prior_art: open as far as checked (4 Nov 2026: catalogue.json and research/leads.json have no Mss/2408, 2409, Villahermosa, Constable, Monterrey 1674 or Borja 1673/79 entry; three web text searches found no edition or study of these ciphered letters). Vols. 3-8 of the series were not looked at and may hold other translations.

leads.title: William Harborne (Constantinople) → Walsingham, letters marked 'undeciphered', with deciphered siblings and a key probably preserved
leads.correspondents: William Harborne → Sir Francis Walsingham
leads.shelfmark: TNA SP 97/1 ff. 54, 56, 58, 62, 66, 75 (Discovery C6766266-C6766275); candidate key SP 106/1 f. 3 (or f. 34)
leads.folio_note: Long letters, e.g. 28 Jun 1584 (21 pp.) and 15 Sep 1584 (33 pp.), per CSP Foreign Eliz. ff. 36, 48, 68, 97 and 113 of the same volume carry period decipherments: a check set.
leads.status: CSP Foreign Eliz. marks these letters 'undeciphered', while other pieces of the same volume carry period decipherments. Conyers Read (Mr Secretary Walsingham, 1925, III, p. 329) says the code was later used with Barton and that its key is in 'P.R.O. Cipher Book, Eliz. i, f. 3' (= SP 106/1); a note there gives f. 34. Barton's SP 97/2 has at least 13 pieces 'and decipher' (1590-92). Not seen by us.
leads.why: The first English embassy to the Ottoman court, reported in cipher to Walsingham in the years before the Armada; this would replace lead 1254, whose letters are printed.

leads.title: Henri III → Bellièvre and Villeroy, Ollainville: cipher postscript (17 lines) and three glossed cipher passages
leads.correspondents: Henri III (countersigned Pinart) → Pomponne de Bellièvre and Nicolas de Neufville de Villeroy
leads.shelfmark: BnF, Français 15906 (2), ff. 520r-522v
leads.folio_note: Gallica btv1b9064322t canvases 92-95 (openings). f. 521r 7 cipher lines and f. 521v 2 + 13 lines, each with the contemporary decipherment in the margin; f. 522v a 17-line cipher postscript after the signature, nothing written beside it
leads.status: Found by the Bellièvre volume sweep, 5 Nov 2026 (research/gallica_sweep/NOTES.md). Homophonic letter substitution with word signs and number codes; key rebuilt from the glossed blocks and the postscript read in part (research/gallica_sweep/bellievre_hi/ps1580/report.md). Printed: Lettres de Henri III t. V (2000) no. 4006, p. 110, an analysis that quotes and summarises the postscript (Biron and the peace, Villeroy to write to him), so its content was deciphered by the editors. Closed as read (edition).
leads.why: Henri III's instructions to his two negotiators on their way to the peace of Fleix: Anjou's troops near Cambrai, Portugal, England and Biron's part in the peace.
leads.score_note: Viewed on the full-resolution Gallica images (openapi.bnf.fr IIIF) during the Bellièvre volume sweep, 5 Nov 2026
